Title: The Walking Grove
Rumor: The Walking Grove. Woodcutters speak of a small grove of ancient trees that appears in a different location every spring. Its trees are unusually tall, and their branches grow together so tightly that sunlight barely reaches the ground. Anyone who marks one of the trunks finds the mark gone by morning, and a few woodsmen claim that the trees move while no one is watching.
First lead: Velthari guides know several clearings where the grove has reportedly appeared.

Title: The Hollow King's Court
Rumor: The Hollow King's Court. Deep within the forest lies a great hollow tree containing a stairway descending beneath its roots. According to an old woodland tale, the stairs lead to the abandoned court of a forgotten king who ruled the forest before the arrival of elves or humans. Those who enter are warned never to accept food offered beneath the earth.
First lead: A Hollowbough story preserves a description of the tree's unusual silver bark.

Title: The Thirteen Rings
Rumor: The Thirteen Rings. An enormous fallen tree lies somewhere beyond the logging camps, its trunk bearing only thirteen growth rings despite being larger than any tree in the surrounding forest. Each ring contains intricate patterns resembling writing. One woodcutter who attempted to remove a section of the trunk returned with his hair turned completely white.
First lead: The tale is often repeated at the Split Stag, where several lumbermen claim to have seen the tree.

Title: The Forgotten Village
Rumor: The Forgotten Village. Hunters sometimes discover the ruins of a small settlement deep within the woods, its buildings overgrown with moss and vines. There are no signs of violence or fire, and the inhabitants appear to have departed suddenly, leaving tools and household possessions behind. Most unsettling is the presence of fresh bread occasionally found upon an abandoned table.
First lead: An old Briarhearth family map marks a village absent from modern surveys.

Title: The Lanterns of the Lost Road
Rumor: The Lanterns of the Lost Road. On misty nights, a line of pale lights appears among the trees, following the course of a road that no longer exists. Travelers who follow the lights sometimes emerge miles from where they began, beside ruined bridges and forgotten boundary stones. Others claim to have encountered processions of silent figures carrying lanterns toward the mountains.
First lead: Independent wagoners know a stretch of abandoned woodland road where the lights most often appear.

Title: The Stag with Thirteen Antlers
Rumor: The Stag with Thirteen Antlers. Velthari tradition describes a magnificent stag bearing thirteen branching antlers, each adorned with pale blossoms. It is said to appear when the forest is threatened, guiding worthy travelers toward places of refuge. Woodcutters who encounter it sometimes discover that their axes have become too heavy to lift until they leave the grove.
First lead: Elder Velthari stories associate the stag with a series of ancient woodland shrines.

Title: The Blackthorn Crown
Rumor: The Blackthorn Crown. A ruined watchpost somewhere in the forest bears carvings of a crown fashioned from twisted thorns. No one knows whether the symbol belongs to a forgotten kingdom, an ancient religious order, or something older. Travelers report that blackthorn bushes bloom around the ruins even in winter, and that their flowers never wither.
First lead: A damaged survey sketch in the Forest Office depicts the watchpost.

Title: The Charcoal Burner's Guest
Rumor: The Charcoal Burner's Guest. An old story tells of a charcoal burner who offered shelter to a strange traveler during a terrible winter. In gratitude, the visitor showed him a hidden place where the forest floor was scattered with silver coins. The burner became wealthy but refused to reveal the location. His abandoned charcoal kiln supposedly still stands beside the trail.
First lead: Descendants of the burner's neighbors remember the approximate location of his former camp.

Title: The Forest That Remembers
Rumor: The Forest That Remembers. A particular stretch of woodland is said to repeat sounds spoken there years or even centuries earlier. Hunters have heard distant battles, children's laughter, and unfamiliar songs among otherwise silent trees. A few believe the phenomenon could reveal what happened to a settlement that disappeared during the War of Broken Banners.
First lead: Hollowbough wardens know the forest by an old name meaning something close to the listening wood.

Title: The Rootbound Chapel
Rumor: The Rootbound Chapel. Deep in the forest stands an abandoned stone chapel almost entirely swallowed by the roots of enormous trees. Its altar remains untouched, and a single candle is said to burn before it on certain holy days. No one knows who tends the flame, although travelers occasionally find offerings of bread and flowers left outside the entrance.
First lead: Briarhearth foresters sometimes speak of the chapel when discussing the oldest woodland trails.

Title: The Sleeping Giant
Rumor: The Sleeping Giant. A long, wooded ridge resembles the figure of a giant lying upon his back. Local tradition maintains that the hill is no natural formation but the body of an ancient forest guardian who fell asleep centuries ago. During violent storms, deep rumbling sounds can be heard beneath the ridge, and the surrounding trees sway even when there is no wind.
First lead: The ridge is visible from a remote logging road, though few camps remain nearby.

Title: The Green Door
Rumor: The Green Door. Woodcutters report finding a narrow green door set into the trunk of an enormous oak, complete with a brass handle and an old-fashioned lock. The door has been seen in several different parts of the forest, but never twice in the same place. One traveler claims to have opened it and found a beautifully furnished room overlooking an unfamiliar landscape.
First lead: A woodcutter at the Logger's Rest possesses a sketch of the door's distinctive carvings.

Title: The Bridge of Bones
Rumor: The Bridge of Bones. Deep in the northeastern woods, an ancient stone bridge spans a narrow ravine. Its parapets are decorated with carvings resembling human and elven bones, and no stream presently flows beneath it. A woodland legend warns that crossing the bridge after sunset allows unseen travelers to follow one home.
First lead: Old Hollowbough boundary stories describe the bridge as a place best avoided.

Title: The Rattleknife's First Treasure
Rumor: The Rattleknife's First Treasure. Goblin bandits have long passed the name Kreech Redcap from one chief to another. According to a popular tale, the original Redcap hid a fortune somewhere in the forest, leaving a series of ridiculous riddles that only another goblin would understand. Every new bearer of the name supposedly searches for the treasure, though none has publicly claimed to find it.
First lead: Spindle Vex is rumored to possess one of the original riddles, or at least a convincing forgery.

Title: The Witch of Alder Run
Rumor: The Witch of Alder Run. An old foresters' tale describes a solitary woman who lived beside the upper reaches of Alder Run, brewing remedies from rare plants and speaking with the animals of the forest. Her cottage disappeared generations ago, but travelers still find neatly arranged bundles of medicinal herbs hanging from branches near the stream. Some believe her descendants continue to inhabit the woods.
First lead: Sister Pera Moss has heard stories from injured lumbermen who claim to have received unexplained help there.

Title: The Last Colours' Burial Ground
Rumor: The Last Colours' Burial Ground. Veterans whisper of a secluded clearing where soldiers of the defeated northern armies buried their dead during the final years of the war. The graves are marked with simple stones and faded scraps of cloth, but one account claims that a sealed iron chest was buried beneath the central memorial. Its contents are said to be more important than gold.
First lead: Former soldiers sometimes recognize an old Galrothe marching song containing directions to the clearing.

Title: The Mirror Pond
Rumor: The Mirror Pond. Somewhere in the deep forest lies a perfectly circular pond whose waters remain still even during storms. Those who gaze into it reportedly see the forest as it appeared centuries earlier, complete with buildings and paths long since vanished. A Hollowbough story warns against entering the water, for the reflection does not always match the present shore.
First lead: Saelis Moonthorn knows an old tale describing the pond's surrounding trees.

Title: The Orchard of Winter Fruit
Rumor: The Orchard of Winter Fruit. Briarhearth families speak of an abandoned orchard where apples ripen beneath snow-covered branches. Its fruit is said to preserve remarkably well, and some elders believe the trees were planted by settlers who made a bargain with a woodland spirit. The orchard has been lost for years, although unusual fruit occasionally appears in the baskets of wandering traders.
First lead: Sela Hallow has heard the orchard mentioned in older Briarhearth family histories.

Title: The Woodcutter's Bell
Rumor: The Woodcutter's Bell. An old iron bell hangs from a branch somewhere in the forest, though no building stands nearby. It reportedly rings whenever a traveler becomes lost, and those who follow the sound sometimes discover a safe trail home. Others claim the bell sounds only before a death among the nearby lumber camps.
First lead: Several independent loggers know a woodland crossroads where the bell was last heard.

Title: The Heartwood Tree
Rumor: The Heartwood Tree. Velthari legends describe an immense tree at the center of an ancient grove, said to be older than any living elder. Its wood is claimed to possess unusual magical properties, but the tree itself is considered sacred and must never be felled. Recently, rumors have spread that someone discovered a freshly broken branch of the Heartwood, large enough to supply several years of rare magical crafting.
First lead: Tavian Briarhand and Maeriel Fenbough have both heard conflicting reports of the branch's discovery.
